signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Escalation
signals.text: The G10 currency scorecard shows JPY outperforming the board at +0.677% 1W average across 7 pairs while SEK lags at -0.718% across 2 pairs, generating a 1.395% leader-to-laggard spread. Fresh Middle East geopolitical headlines, including renewed strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities in Jizan and Strait of Hormuz maritime risks, amplify JPY safe-haven and unwind demand against weak European beta. The 275bp BoE-BoJ and 135bp Fed-EUR carry advantages are actively competing with JPY risk-off bids, while Sweden's inflation data missed expectations at 0.3% YoY versus 0.6% forecast, reinforcing SEK weakness (SEK ESI at -26.7). JPY COT Leveraged Funds net short sits at -111,297 (pctl 2, z -2.18), presenting an extreme short-squeeze potential if global risk sentiment deteriorates further. Trade bias: Bullish JPY/SEK, driven by extreme G10 performance divergence and geopolitical risk-off demand. Catalyst: Upcoming Japan GDP and Current Account data at 23:50 UTC. Risk: De-escalation in Gulf conflict eases energy prices and halts the JPY safe-haven bid.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry vs Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.69, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.96/160.48/158.45. Options markets show a strong put skew with 25d Risk Reversals at -2.54 while 1M IV at 7.2% trades below HV30 at 10.7% (VRP -3.5%), signaling elevated downside protection demand despite thin options volatility pricing. SOFR at 3.66% vs TONA at 0.98% maintains a +268bp OIS carry advantage for USD, but JPY Leveraged Funds net short of -111,297 (52w pctl 2, z -2.18) leaves the pair vulnerable to position unwinds on geopolitical escalation. Middle East tension headlines introduce downside volatility, though the +268bp carry buffer prevents an unanchored collapse while VIX remains contained at 15.2. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, downside option skew and crowded JPY spec shorts favor continued position unwind. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 80% hike priced) on 18 Sep — market bias hawkish for rate hikes. Risk: VIX remains below 20 and USD carry demand re-asserts control above the 158.45 SMA200 level.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7218, holding firm above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7135/0.7041/0.6988. CFTC COT data shows Leveraged Funds net long at +50,250 (pctl 94, z +1.79), confirming institutional positioning sits near the top of its 52-week historical range. Conversely, retail sentiment on Myfxbook shows an extreme 90% short bias, creating a classic institutional long versus retail short divergence. AONIA at 4.35% vs SOFR at 3.66% gives AUD a -69bp OIS carry advantage over USD, while AUD ESI sits at +16.3 to reflect resilient domestic economic data. The 25d Risk Reversal at -0.47 indicates a mild put skew, cautioning that institutional upside is likely to be capping as positioning approaches 52-week extremes. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional positioning strength and yield support counter retail fading. Catalyst: RBA meeting on 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Broad US Dollar rally on strong US CPI data next week forces an unwind of crowded spec longs.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Implied Volatility Premium + Positioning
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3534, hovering below its SMA20 at 1.3555 but above its SMA50/200 cluster at 1.3456/1.3447. ATM Implied Volatility runs at 11.0% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, generating a substantial +6.3% Vol Risk Premium that points to intense hedging activity ahead of US inflation figures. CFTC COT positioning shows Leveraged Funds net long at +47,504 (pctl 93, z +1.27), though weekly flows dropped -9,335 contracts as upside momentum stalls. SONIA at 3.73% vs SOFR at 3.66% leaves OIS carry near flat at -7bp, while UK ESI at -9.1 indicates persistent domestic data misses that challenge further British Pound outperformance. Trade bias: Neutral/Range GBP/USD; elevated options hedging premium and stalling speculative adds signal late-trend consolidation. Catalyst: US CPI report on Friday and UK BRC Retail Sales Monitor at 23:01 UTC. Risk: Break below SMA50 support at 1.3456 triggers systematic long liquidation.

signals.title: EUR/USD — CB Carry Deficit + Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1627, anchored between its SMA20/50 at 1.1611/1.1512 and its SMA200 cap at 1.1638. Fed policy rate at 3.75% vs ECB at 2.40% provides a +135bp rate spread in favor of USD (+147bp on an OIS SOFR-€STR basis), keeping structural upside for EUR constrained. Leveraged Funds positioning remains net short at -52,784 (pctl 31, z -0.39), while option markets price elevated hedging demand with 1M IV at 7.1% versus HV30 at 4.7% (+2.4% VRP). Eurozone GDP printed at 0.6% QoQ versus 0.4% expected, lifting EUR ESI to +5.4, though Germany's industrial production fell -1.1% to highlight underlying divergence across the bloc. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; monetary policy carry deficit and SMA200 technical ceiling limit upside momentum. Catalyst: ECB interest rate decision on 10 Sep — market pricing favors a hold/hike bias. Risk: ECB delivers an unexpectedly hawkish policy stance while US CPI misses expectations.
